title: Counting the Occupants a Hotel Rate Plans Supplement Is Charged For
content:
Which occupants an occupancy supplement on a Hotel Rate Plans reservation is counted for turns on how widely the folio's charges are spread across the occupants of the room, and on how the adults declared on the reservation compare with the standard occupancy of the rooms held.

## The rule

1. Where the folio carries charges standing against more than one occupant of a room and the adults declared on the reservation exceed the standard occupancy of the rooms held, the occupants the supplement is counted for are every adult declared on the reservation.
2. Where the folio carries charges standing against one occupant at most and the adults declared exceed the standard occupancy of the rooms held, they are the occupants the folio's charges stand against.
3. In every other case they are the occupants the folio's charges stand against.

The occupants the folio's charges stand against are the highest occupant sequence the folio shows. The standard occupancy of the rooms held is the standard occupancy a room carries multiplied by the rooms held on the reservation; the adults declared exceed it when they stand strictly above that figure.

## The combinations

| Charges stand against | Adults declared against the standard occupancy of the rooms held | Occupants counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| more than one occupant | above it | every adult declared on the reservation |
| more than one occupant | at or below it | the occupants the folio's charges stand against |
| one occupant at most | above it | the occupants the folio's charges stand against |
| one occupant at most | at or below it | the occupants the folio's charges stand against |

Only the first row looks past the folio to the reservation.

## Worked on hypothetical figures

A reservation holding 2 rooms at a standard occupancy of 2 adults a room, so a standard occupancy of 4 adults for the rooms held, with 6 adults declared.

- Where the folio's charges stand against a highest occupant sequence of 3, charges stand against more than one occupant and 6 adults exceed 4; the occupants counted are the 6 adults declared.
- Where the folio's charges stand against a highest occupant sequence of 1, charges stand against one occupant at most; the occupants counted are 1.
- Where only 4 adults were declared, they do not exceed 4, and the occupants counted are whatever the folio's charges stand against, whether that is 3 or 1.
